findings.summary: The required-field scan ignores negation, so an edit that negates a naming instruction passes.
findings.evidence: The plan rejects requiring a non-negated anchor because the D63 sentence (verifier.md line 7) holds `unless`. As a result, an edit that negates the instruction itself, such as 'Do not list them in commands' or 'Never record it in request_reading_mismatch', still satisfies the anchor. The forbidden patterns do not cover it either, so the most direct contradiction of D43's instruction is accepted. Fix: For the anchor scan, treat a clause as negated only by a narrower set (not, never, cannot, no, n't words) that excludes `unless`. The shipped D63 sentence holds only `unless` and `unmet`, so it still passes. Add a test that 'Do not list them in commands exactly as run' in place of the original is refused with D43.

findings.summary: A negator anywhere in a clause excuses it, even when it strengthens the contradiction.
findings.evidence: A clause counts as negated if it holds any negator anywhere, so a negator that strengthens the claim excuses it: 'Accept uncited commands with no exceptions' and 'A partly run command counts unless told otherwise' both pass. These are plain contradictions that a reviewer would expect a screen to catch. Fix: Count a negator only when it appears before the last matched pattern word in the clause. This keeps 'No record made on another tree counts', 'Neither ... nor ... counts' and 'evidence text alone is not enough' accepted and refuses the examples above. Add one of them to the refusal tests.
findings.location: Decision 3 (negation by any negator in the clause)

findings.summary: The drift guard does not say to strip the `//!` markers, so the D115 phrase that spans two header lines would not be found.
findings.evidence: The D115 source 'Athena ran and recorded it on the same candidate tree and it passed' spans verify.rs lines 7-8 ('...or Athena ran and' / '//! recorded it on...'). Step 7 says to take the lines starting `//!` and collapse whitespace, but it does not say to strip the `//!` marker. Joining the raw lines gives 'ran and //! recorded', and the guard fails. Fix: State that each header line has its leading `//!` removed before joining with single spaces and collapsing whitespace.

findings.summary: reading.rs is listed as a deliverable but is deliberately left unchanged.
findings.evidence: The brief lists crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as a deliverable to modify, while criterion 9 and the reading's assumptions say it is deliberately unchanged. The plan resolves this correctly and raises it as an open question. Fix: No change needed beyond keeping the open question. The verifier should not count the untouched reading.rs as a missing deliverable.

summary: I read the plan against verify.rs, the three verifier prompts, lib.rs, code_health.rs, xtask policy.rs and athena.toml, and it holds up. The items it names exist: `judge` at verify.rs:408 runs to 675, the D43 format! string is at 601, the mismatch finding is built with `.into()` at 631-635, `mod tests` starts at 1141, the mismatch test is at 2666, and VERIFIER_FRAME at context lib.rs:50 is the raw verifier.md. I walked the planned clause rules over the real text by hand: all three shipped prompts pass, all five planned edits are refused, and the three deletion cases are caught (`in commands` exists only in 'list them in commands'). The enforcement point is real. athena.toml says the test check never skips, so a candidate that edits only a prompt still runs the whole workspace `cargo test`. The include_str! of the fragments goes only in the test module. That matters because the athena-bin cache-key scan in policy.rs (`compiled_in_files`) reads only the code before `#[cfg(test)]`, so it is unaffected. The dependents list covers the readers I found that read verify.rs as text (the admission.rs test and the refusal_corpus fixture), the CHANGELOG readers and the code_health limits. Three minor weak spots remain. (1) The required-field scan ignores negation, so 'Do not list them in commands' passes. (2) A negator anywhere in a clause excuses it, so 'accept uncited commands with no exceptions' passes. (3) The drift guard's haystack must strip the `//!` markers before joining lines, or the D115 phrase, which spans header lines 7-8, is not found. None of these blocks a criterion, and the plan states the word-set limits.
